3: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × (6/7)h × h = 3h²/7.
4: The square has area 81, so its side is 9. Each triangle's perimeter 30 includes one 9-side of the square, so its two outer sides add to 21. The outline is made of the 4 pairs of outer sides: 4 × 21 = 84.
5: Each triangle has the angle n at the crossing (vertically opposite angles are equal), so its two marked angles add to 180° − n. Two triangles: 2(180° − n) = 360° − 2n.
6: Opposite (vertical) angles are equal, so the six angles form three equal pairs, and the three different values add to 180°. t and z are vertically opposite — knowing both gives only one value, which is not enough. Every other pair gives two different values, and the third follows.
7: X is symmetric about a vertical and a horizontal line (and its diagonals). K, L, M and Y each have at most one line of symmetry.
8: Count the small squares: Figure A has 13, so each is 26 ÷ 13 = 2 cm². Figure B has 8 squares: 8 × 2 = 16 cm².
9: The altitude makes two right triangles. Right part: 2y + 40 = 90, so y = 25. Left part: y + z = 90, so z = 65.
10: In an isosceles triangle the line from the apex to the midpoint of the base is also the altitude and the angle bisector: so x = y, w = z, AD = DC and BD ⊥ AC all hold. w and x are different angles with no reason to be equal (w + x = 90°).
11: The three lines form a triangle with one angle z = 30°, so its other two angles sum to 150°. x and y are the angles next to those two on straight lines: x + y = (180 − a) + (180 − b) = 360 − 150 = 210.
12: Below line AB there are five angles marked x: 5x = 180, x = 36. Above it: y + 2x = 180, so y = 180 − 72 = 108.
